title: Boss: deploys, bans and double charges
summary: A worker that drains properly on shutdown, a client that honours Retry-After, and payments that are safe to retry.

steps.title: The ticket
body: **INC-7210: three problems from one bad week in payments.**
Mon 10:02 fail: Worker[0] System.OperationCanceledException: The operation was canceled.
Wed 15:40 warn: Partner[0] 429 Too Many Requests, Retry-After: 2   (retrying in 37 ms)
Wed 15:41 crit: Partner[0] 403 Forbidden: API key suspended for abuse
Fri 09:13 info: Payments[0] charged order 5521 (key 7f3a...)    # client timeout, then retry
Fix the worker's shutdown, make the partner client wait as long as the partner asks, and make `PayAsync` idempotent.

steps.title: 1. Drain, do not drop
prompt: Write **`static async Task<int> RunWorkerAsync(System.Threading.Channels.ChannelReader<string> jobs, Func<string, Task> handle, CancellationToken stopping)`**:
- handle jobs one at a time until the channel is completed and empty, and return how many were handled;
- when `stopping` is cancelled: **finish the job in progress** (do not abandon it), **start no new job**, and return the count
The tests cancel `stopping` while the first job is in progress.
starter: static async Task<int> RunWorkerAsync(System.Threading.Channels.ChannelReader<string> jobs, Func<string, Task> handle, CancellationToken stopping)
solution: static async Task<int> RunWorkerAsync(System.Threading.Channels.ChannelReader<string> jobs, Func<string, Task> handle, CancellationToken stopping)
await handle(job);   // no token: a started job is finished
// shutting down while waiting for work: nothing in progress
template: async Task DojoHandle(string job) { dojoStarted.Add(job); if (job == "j1") { dojoInJ1.SetResult(); await dojoGate.Task; } dojoFinished.Add(job); }
await Dojo.TryAsync("Shutdown does not throw", async () => { dojoCount = await dojoRun; });
Dojo.Eq("The job in progress was finished", new List<string> { "j1" }, dojoFinished);
Dojo.Eq("No new job started after the stop", new List<string> { "j1" }, dojoStarted);
Dojo.Eq("It reports one job handled", 1, dojoCount);
Dojo.Eq("Without a stop, it drains the channel", 3, await RunWorkerAsync(dojoCh2.Reader, _ => Task.CompletedTask, CancellationToken.None));
await Dojo.TryAsync("Stopping an idle worker returns quietly", async () => Dojo.Eq("An idle worker handled nothing", 0, await dojoIdle));
hints: `ReadAllAsync(stopping)` throws as soon as `stopping` is cancelled. Use `WaitToReadAsync(stopping)` and `TryRead`, and check `stopping` before taking each job.
Wrap the loop in `try { ... } catch (OperationCanceledException) when (stopping.IsCancellationRequested) { }` for the case where the worker was idle.

steps.title: 2. Wait as long as you are told
prompt: The partner answers `429` with `Retry-After`. Our client retried after a few milliseconds, again and again, and the partner suspended
our key. The tests define `RateLimitedException` with a `TimeSpan RetryAfter`.
Write **`static async Task<T> CallAsync<T>(Func<CancellationToken, Task<T>> op, int maxAttempts, Func<TimeSpan, CancellationToken, Task> delay, CancellationToken ct)`**:
- on `RateLimitedException`, wait **exactly** `RetryAfter` with `delay(retryAfter, ct)` and try again, up to `maxAttempts` calls
in total; after that, let the last `RateLimitedException` out;
- any other exception goes out at once.
starter: static async Task<T> CallAsync<T>(Func<CancellationToken, Task<T>> op, int maxAttempts, Func<TimeSpan, CancellationToken, Task> delay, CancellationToken ct)
solution: static async Task<T> CallAsync<T>(Func<CancellationToken, Task<T>> op, int maxAttempts, Func<TimeSpan, CancellationToken, Task> delay, CancellationToken ct)
template: Task DojoDelay(TimeSpan d, CancellationToken ct) { dojoWaits.Add(d); return Task.CompletedTask; }
Dojo.Eq("It succeeds after two 429s", "quote 42", await CallAsync(DojoPartner, 5, DojoDelay, CancellationToken.None));
Dojo.Eq("It waited exactly what Retry-After said", new List<TimeSpan> { TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2), TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5) }, dojoWaits);
Task<string> DojoAlways429(CancellationToken ct) { dojoCalls++; return Task.FromException<string>(new RateLimitedException(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1))); }
await Dojo.ThrowsAsync<RateLimitedException>("It gives up after maxAttempts", () => CallAsync(DojoAlways429, 3, DojoDelay, CancellationToken.None));
Task<string> DojoForbidden(CancellationToken ct) { dojoCalls++; return Task.FromException<string>(new UnauthorizedAccessException("403")); }
await Dojo.ThrowsAsync<UnauthorizedAccessException>("Other errors are not retried", () => CallAsync(DojoForbidden, 5, DojoDelay, CancellationToken.None));
class RateLimitedException(TimeSpan retryAfter) : Exception("429 Too Many Requests")
hints: Catch only `RateLimitedException`, with an exception filter on the attempt number.
`catch (RateLimitedException e) when (attempt < maxAttempts) { await delay(e.RetryAfter, ct); }`

steps.title: 3. Charge once per key
prompt: Write **`PaymentHandler(Func<string, Task<string>> charge)`** with **`Task<string> PayAsync(string idempotencyKey, string order)`**:
- the first call with a key runs `charge(order)` and returns its receipt;
- any later call with the same key, **including one that arrives while the first is still running**, returns the same receipt
- if the charge **fails**, the caller gets the exception and the key is **not** remembered, so a retry may charge.
starter: public async Task<string> PayAsync(string idempotencyKey, string order)
if (_receipts.TryGetValue(idempotencyKey, out var receipt)) return receipt;
solution: public async Task<string> PayAsync(string idempotencyKey, string order)
template: Dojo.Eq("A retry during the first call does not charge again", 1, dojoCharges);
Dojo.Eq("Both get the same receipt", dojoR1, dojoR2);
Dojo.Eq("A later retry gets the stored receipt", dojoR1, await dojoPay.PayAsync("key-1", "order-5521"));
Dojo.Eq("A new key charges", "receipt 2 for order-9", await dojoPay.PayAsync("key-2", "order-9"));
await Dojo.ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException>("A failed charge reaches the caller", () => dojoPay.PayAsync("key-3", "declined"));
await Dojo.ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException>("A retry after a failure charges again", () => dojoPay.PayAsync("key-3", "declined"));
hints: Two callers with the same key must share one charge: store a `Lazy<Task<string>>` per key with `GetOrAdd`.
Await `lazy.Value`; on failure `TryRemove(KeyValuePair.Create(key, lazy))` and rethrow.
explain: In production the key store is a database table with a unique index on the key (and the request hash, to reject a reused key
with a different body), written in the same transaction as the payment. The in-memory version teaches the shape; the database
makes it survive restarts and work across replicas.
